title: Small Cohen–Macaulay modules
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's counterexample (2026) to the domain form of the small Cohen-Macaulay module conjecture: a three-dimensional complete Noetherian normal local domain containing C, with residue field C, that has no nonzero finitely generated module of depth three. The ring is the completed cone over a Hirzebruch-Kummer surface. The proof is given in full from five named hypotheses on smooth projective surfaces: Chern classes and Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch for coherent sheaves, Noether's formula, Bogomolov's inequality, the plane blown up at four points, and Euler numbers. The first lesson constructs completed cones over surfaces with a regular model and shows how a small Cohen-Macaulay module gives a torsion-free sheaf on the exceptional surface. The second proves the Harder-Narasimhan filtration, a balancing by elementary modifications, and a variance inequality for sheaves on the plane that extend trivially. The third combines Riemann-Roch, Bogomolov's inequality, the Hodge index theorem and Noether's formula into the obstruction K_X^2 - 2c_2(X) <= 6H^2. The fourth constructs a cover of the blown-up plane with K_X^2 - 2c_2(X) > 6H^2.
prerequisites: course Commutative algebra for geometry: completion, faithful flatness, integral extensions, regular local rings, depth and Cohen-Macaulay modules, the Auslander-Buchsbaum formula

courses Morphisms of schemes and Cohomology of quasi-coherent sheaves: finite and proper morphisms, Zariski's main theorem, ample invertible sheaves, normalization, Serre's theorems, flat base change, Euler characteristics and Hilbert polynomials
course Flat, smooth and étale morphisms, lesson on étale morphisms (Theorem 5.1)
course ℓ-adic cohomology and trace formulas, lesson on cycle classes: the intersection pairing on a surface, surface Riemann-Roch for line bundles, the Hodge index theorem
the lessons prove every other fact they use, except the named hypotheses (CS) of the second lesson, (NF) and (BI) of the third, (BL) and (EU) of the fourth, and the related work quoted in the first

checks.reading: The manuscript 'A Complete Local Domain without a Small Cohen-Macaulay Module' (OpenAI, 23 Sep 2026, repository commit adc7f124; seven sections, one figure, paper.tex 698 lines and surface.tex 337 lines) was read in full on 14 Oct 2026, and every step of its argument was derived again while the lessons were written: the finite map to the plane; the section ring, its completion and its dimension; the regular model, its regularity and integrality, the global functions and normality; freeness over the power series ring and local freeness on the puncture; the reflexive extension and the torsion-freeness of its restriction; the Harder-Narasimhan filtration; the Tor computation and the termination of the balancing; the variance inequality with its layers, the K_0 identity and the final identity; the comparison of the two Riemann-Roch polynomials, the Bogomolov, Hodge index and Noether steps; the mixture; the complete quadrangle, Kummer theory, the valuation vectors and the local form; the canonical class, the Euler number, the polarization and its ampleness; the uncompleted local ring. No error found. Differences of presentation, none a correction: the degree of the map to the plane is computed from two Riemann-Roch polynomials; Chern classes on the plane are defined through Hilbert polynomials, so that Riemann-Roch on the plane, the positivity of c_1 of globally generated sheaves and the variance inequality need no hypothesis; the Harder-Narasimhan filtration is proved from (CS); N = rh is read off from the degree of the cover; the ampleness of -K_B and of H is proved with the finite morphism given by a globally generated bundle and Serre's cohomological criterion in place of the Nakai-Moishezon criterion; the projection formula for pullbacks along the cover is derived from (CS); normalization commutes with the étale base change by the programme's lesson on étale morphisms. Observations added, each with its proof: the incidence graph of the branch divisor is the Petersen graph; n = 7 is the smallest prime for which the obstruction applies; chi(O_X) = n^3(7n^2 - 30n + 35)/12; a balancing to slope width lambda would give K_X^2 - 2c_2(X) <= 3(1 + lambda^2)H^2. open_obligations: Named hypothesis (CS): Chern classes c_1 and ch_2 of coherent sheaves on a smooth projective surface, additive, compatible with twists, with c_1 of sheaves of rank zero nonnegative on ample classes, and Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch. Not proved in the programme (stated in Reid, Chapter B, item ix). Used for slopes, the Harder-Narasimhan filtration and the balancing, Lemma 2.1 of the third lesson, and the projection formula of the fourth.
Named hypothesis (NF): Noether's formula 12 chi(O_X) = K_X^2 + c_2(X), with c_2(X) the topological Euler number. Not proved in the programme (stated in Reid, Chapter B, item ix).

Named hypothesis (BI): Bogomolov's inequality 2u ch_2(G) <= c_1(G)^2 for torsion-free slope-semistable sheaves on a smooth projective complex surface. Not proved in the programme (statement read in Langer, arXiv:2107.03125, Theorem 3.13).

Named hypothesis (BL): the plane blown up at four points, no three collinear (Picard group, intersection form, canonical class, strict transforms of lines, Euler number 7). Not proved in the programme (Reid, Chapter 1, Section 1.10).

Named hypothesis (EU): Euler characteristics with compact supports are additive over closed subsets and multiplicative in finite étale covers, and equal the topological Euler number for smooth projective varieties. Not proved in the programme (Behrend, arXiv:math/0507523, Section 1.3).

The programme results on commutative algebra, schemes and cohomology that are used are cited with their numbers; their proofs were not checked again for this course. The lessons on cycle classes and on étale morphisms are by other authors of the programme.
The related work in Section 1 of the first lesson (Hochster's dimension-two result; the preprints of Anghel and Chen) is quoted, not checked.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
